key_finding: A BiLSTM-attention model inside a five-dimensional cold-chain digital twin, using one pallet-level sensor, predicts in-box fruit temperature within ±0.3 °C (about 60% error reduction vs ambient-only), giving shelf-life errors under ±1.2 days and simulated food-loss reductions of 8.6-15.5%; box-level twins are the most precise unit.

quotes.text: The VFC is a digital mirror of the PFC, comprising geometric, physical, behavioral, and rule-based models to simulate real-world conditions and predict food quality under various scenarios
quotes.section: 2.1 Architecture of digital twin enabled cold supply chains

quotes.text: The experiment replicated a typical fresh-produce cold chain, comprising pre-cooling, cold storage, refrigerated transport, and loading/unloading (temperature breaks).

In the first stage, multi-source data—including experimental temperature measurements, food attributes, and equipment/environmental parameters—were used to train a Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) model with an attention mechanism to minimize temperature prediction error.
The AS provides functional and business tools for real-time decision-making, enabling users to monitor, manage, and optimize supply chain activities.

quotes.text: Ultimately, this model reduces food loss by approximately 8.6 %–15.5 % among the fruit types tested, outperforming both static shelf-life assumptions and simpler ambient-based methods.
Future efforts can refine this approach by incorporating additional management systems (e.g., anomaly detection and logistics optimization)
